answer: The echo multiplier is published, charged in ocean, and harbor lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1762 identities would post 3916 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
